questions.stem:
The mass of iron converted into $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ by the action of $18$ g of steam is :
(Given : Molar mass of H, O and Fe are $1$, $16$ and $56\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively)
Assume iron is present in excess :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{3Fe + 4H_2O \rightarrow Fe_3O_4 + 4H_2}$
$\because$ 4 mole $\mathrm{H_2O}$ react with 3 mole Fe
$\therefore$ for 1 mole $\mathrm{H_2O}$ we need $\frac{3}{4}$ mole Fe
mass of $\mathrm{Fe} = \frac{3}{4} \times 56 = 42\ \mathrm{g}$

questions.stem:
What is the energy (in $\mathrm{J\ atom^{-1}}$) required for the following process?
$\mathrm{Li^{2+}(g) \rightarrow Li^{3+}(g) + e^{-}}$
(Take the ionization energy for the H atom in the ground state as $2.18 \times 10^{-18}\ \mathrm{J\ atom^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{IE = IE_H \times Z^{2}}$
$= 2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times Z^{2}\ \mathrm{J/atom}$
$= 2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times (3)^{2}$
$= 1.96 \times 10^{-17}\ \mathrm{J/atom}$

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The correct sequence of bond lengths in the following species is :
$\mathrm{O_2^{+} < O_2 < O_2^{-} < O_2^{2-}}$
Statement (II) : The correct sequence of number of unpaired electrons in the following species is :
$\mathrm{O_2 > O_2^{+} > O_2^{-} > O_2^{2-}}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Species | B.O. | Unpaired $\mathrm{e^{-}}$
$\mathrm{O_2^{+}}$ | 2.5 | 1
$\mathrm{O_2}$ | 2.0 | 2
$\mathrm{O_2^{-}}$ | 1.5 | 1
$\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ | 1.0 | 0
true (I) $\mathrm{B.O.} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{B.L.}}$
B.L : $\mathrm{O_2^{+} < O_2 < O_2^{-} < O_2^{2-}}$
false (II) Unpaired $\mathrm{e^{-}}$ : $\mathrm{O_2 > O_2^{+} = O_2^{-} > O_2^{-}}$

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.stem:
Consider the following data.
(i) $\mathrm{2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 3H_2(g) + 1200\ kJ/mol}$
(ii) $\mathrm{H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2HCl(g) + 164\ kJ/mol}$
(iii) $\mathrm{HCl(g) + aq \rightarrow HCl(aq) + 83\ kJ/mol}$
(iv) $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6(s) + aq \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 663\ kJ/mol}$
The enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6}$ is :
questions.solution:
(i) $\mathrm{2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 3H_2(g)};\ \Delta H_1 = -1200\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$
(ii) $\mathrm{H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2HCl(g)};\ \Delta H_2 = -164\ \mathrm{kJ}$
(iii) $\mathrm{HCl(g) + aq \rightarrow HCl(aq)};\ \Delta H_3 = -83\ \mathrm{kJ}$
(iv) $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6(s) + aq \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq)};\ \Delta H_4 = -663\ \mathrm{kJ}$
$\mathrm{2Al(s) + 3Cl_2(g) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(s)}$  $\Delta H_f = ?$
$\Delta H_f = (1) + 3 \times (2) + 6 \times (3) - (4)$
$= \Delta H_1 + 3(\Delta H_2) + 6(\Delta H_3) - \Delta H_4$
$= -1527\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$

questions.stem: $19.5$ g of fluoro acetic acid (molar mass $78\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) is dissolved in $500$ g of water at $298$ K. The depression in the freezing point of water was $1^\circ\mathrm{C}$. What is $K_a$ of fluoro acetic acid ? (For water, $K_f = 1.86\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$). Assume molarity and molality to have same values.
questions.solution:
$m = \dfrac{\frac{19.5}{78}}{0.5} = 0.5\ \mathrm{mol/kg}$
$\Delta T_f = iK_fm$
$1 = i \times 1.86 \times 0.5$
$i = 1.0753 = 1 + (2 - 1)\alpha$
$\alpha = 0.0753$
$k_a = \frac{c\alpha^{2}}{1 - \alpha} \approx c\alpha^{2}$
$k_a = 0.5 \times (0.0753)^{2} = 3 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.stem:
The solubility product constants of $\mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}$ and $\mathrm{AgBr}$ are $32x$ and $4y$ respectively at $298$ K.
The value of $\left(\dfrac{\text{molarity of } \mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}}{\text{molarity of } \mathrm{AgBr}}\right)$ can be expressed as :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4 \rightleftharpoons 2Ag^{+} + CrO_4^{2-}}$ ($2s_1$, $s_1$)
$K_{sp} = 4s_1^{3} = 32x$
$s_1 = 2\sqrt[3]{x}$
$\mathrm{AgBr \rightleftharpoons Ag^{+} + Br^{-}}$ ($s_2$, $s_2$)
$K_{sp} = s_2^{2} = 4y$
$s_2 = 2\sqrt{y}$
$\frac{s_1}{s_2} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$

questions.stem:
An electrochemical cell is constructed using half cells in the direction of spontaneous change
$\mathrm{Fe(OH)_2(s) + 2e^{-} \rightarrow Fe(s) + 2OH^{-}(aq)}$  $E^\ominus = -0.88\ \mathrm{V}$
and $\mathrm{AgBr(s) + e^{-} \rightarrow Ag(s) + Br^{-}(aq)}$  $E^\ominus = +0.07\ \mathrm{V}$
Which of the following option is correct ?
questions.solution:
For spontaneous cell
Cathode : $\mathrm{AgBr(s) + e^{-} \longrightarrow Ag(s) + Br^{-}(aq)}$
Anode : $\mathrm{Fe(s) + 2OH^{-}(aq) \longrightarrow Fe(OH)_2(s) + 2e^{-}}$
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{cell}} = E^\circ_C - E^\circ_A$
$= 0.07 - (-0.88) = +0.95\ \mathrm{V}$
Cell Rxn :
$\mathrm{Fe(s) + 2OH^{-}(aq) + 2AgBr(s) \longrightarrow Fe(OH)_2(s) + 2Ag(s) + 2Br^{-}(aq)}$
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{cell}}$ is intensive property

options.text: Fe is reduced in the electrochemical cell

questions.stem: $t_{100\%}$ is the time required for the $100\%$ completion of the reaction while $t_{1/2}$ is the time required for $50\%$ of the reaction to be completed. Which of the following option correctly represents the relation between $t_{100\%}$ and $t_{1/2}$ for zero and first order reactions respectively ?
questions.solution:
Zero order : $[\mathrm{A}]_0 - [\mathrm{A}]_t = kt$
$t_{100\%} = \frac{[\mathrm{A}]_0}{k},\ t_{50\%} = \frac{[\mathrm{A}]_0}{2k}$
$\Rightarrow t_{100\%} = 2t_{\frac{1}{2}}$
1st order : $[\mathrm{A}]_t = [\mathrm{A}]_0\,e^{-kt}$ (1st order never completes)
$t_{100\%} = \infty$ or $\left(t_{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{\infty}$

questions.stem:
$5.33$ g of $\mathrm{CrCl_3 \cdot 6H_2O}$, which is a $1 : 3$ electrolyte, is dissolved in water and is passed through a cation exchanger. The chloride ions in the eluted solution, on treatment with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ results in $8.61$ g of AgCl. The ratio of moles of complex reacted and moles of AgCl formed is ______ $\times 10^{-2}$. (Nearest integer)
[Molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ Cr : $52$, Ag : $108$, Cl : $35.5$, H : $1$, O : $16$]
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3 + \underset{excess}{AgNO_3} \rightarrow 3AgCl\downarrow}$
moles of $\mathrm{CrCl_3\cdot 6H_2O} = \frac{5.33}{266.5} = 0.02$
moles of $\mathrm{AgCl} = \frac{8.61}{143.5} = 0.06$
Ratio $= \frac{0.02}{0.06} = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.3333$
$= 33.33 \times 10^{-2} \approx 33 \times 10^{-2}$

questions.stem: One mole of an alkane ($x$) requires $8$ mole oxygen for complete combustion. Sum of number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the alkane ($x$)_______.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}} + \left(\frac{3n+1}{2}\right)\mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow n\mathrm{CO_2} + (n+1)\mathrm{H_2}$
$\frac{3n+1}{2} = 8$
$n = 5$
So $\rightarrow \mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$
Total $= 5 + 12 = 17$

Given : $\log 2 = 0.30, \log 3 = 0.48, R = 8.3\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}, \ln 10 = 2.3$

At the transition temperature T, $\mathrm{A \rightleftharpoons B}$ and $\Delta G^{0} = 105 - 35\log$ where A and B are two states of substance X. The transition temperature in $^\circ\mathrm{C}$ when pressure is $1$ atm is ________.

At the transition Temp (T)
